paras: The shooting of Ross Moore was a robbery and shooting of a Black taxi driver by three young white men on the outskirts of Birmingham, Alabama, in the early morning of February 26, 1919. Moore was shot in the head and left in his car, and when the only known report was filed it was not known whether he would survive.

About 3 a.m., three young white men hired Moore, described as a "Colored taxi driver," at Birmingham's Terminal station and told him to drive them to Mt. Pinson, near Tarrant City. "Far out on the road," according to the dispatch, the passengers shot him in the head, robbed him and left him in the car. Some Black residents found him about 3:30 and drove him in his own car to Hillman hospital, where he arrived in "a supposedly dying condition."
Late the following night his condition was still reported as very serious. The coverage does not name the three men or report any arrest, and no later report of Moore's recovery or death was found.

The case is known from a single Birmingham dispatch dated February 27, which the Cleveland Advocate printed on page 8 of its March 1 issue. The Advocate ran it without comment under the headline "TAXI DRIVER MURDERED," even though the text itself left Moore's survival open. The item identified the victim as "Colored" and his assailants as "young white men" but did not attribute a racial motive, treating the attack as a robbery.
The headline calls Moore "murdered," while the dispatch beneath it says only that "it is not known whether he will survive or not."

accounts.label: Birmingham dispatch
accounts.gist: Three young white men hired Moore at the Terminal station, had him drive toward Mt. Pinson, shot him in the head, robbed him and left him; Black residents found him and took him to hospital.

framing.detail: The Cleveland Advocate ran the dispatch without comment under the headline 'TAXI DRIVER MURDERED', identifying Moore as 'Colored' and his assailants as 'young white men'.

versions.value: Alive in very serious condition, survival unknown (body text)

conflicts.note: The headline and the dispatch text in the same item disagree; the text is the more specific statement and was written as of a late hour the night after the shooting.
